bib.title: Focused Transformer: Contrastive Training for Context Scaling

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Focused Transformer: Contrastive Training for Context Scaling", Szymon Tworkowski, Konrad Staniszewski, Mikołaj Pacek, Yuhuai Wu, Henryk Michalewski, Piotr Miłoś. NeurIPS 2023 (37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems). arXiv:2307.03170v2, 30 Nov 2023.

COVERAGE: All 90,587 chars were extracted and read. I read the main text, the appendices (A–G, plus the Appendix B and C text), the results tables and the limitations section. I skimmed the references and did not read Appendices H–L in detail (datasets, hardware, randomness, extra arXiv perplexity tables 10–11, pseudocode). The figures were not viewed. Plot values are not in the text, so I quote only numbers stated in the text or tables.

CLAIMS (ranked)

- Claim: Under standard training, attention mass spreads evenly over relevant and irrelevant documents. The authors call this the "distraction issue" and say it worsens as memory grows.
  - number: positive attention mass r_d ≈ 1/d.
  - setup: 184M-parameter, 12-layer decoder-only model, memory layer 8. At evaluation the model sees the previous local context plus contexts from d−1 other documents. Compared FoT at several d against a standard Transformer (Fig. 3).
  - quote: "We observe that rd ≈ 1/d, which can be interpreted as the fact that the attention is equally distracted by the positive (coming from the current document at i = 1) and negative keys."
  - where: §3.3, p.5.

- Claim: Crossbatch training mostly fixes the distraction issue. It adds negative keys from other documents, trained differentiably, with no extra loss.
  - number: d ≤ 8 early, then d ≥ 64.
  - setup: the only new hyperparameter is d, the ratio of positive to negative contexts. Starting with small d keeps the model from ignoring the previous local context.
  - quote: "Typically, we find it beneficial to start with small d ≤ 8 (otherwise, the model tends to ignore the previous local context) and later switch to bigger values, say d ≥ 64."
  - where: §3.2, p.5.

- Claim: LongLLaMA 3B, fine-tuned with FoT at 8k context, extrapolates on passkey retrieval far past its training length. The baseline cannot go beyond 2k.
  - number: 94.5% at 100k tokens, 73% at 256k.
  - setup: OpenLLaMA-3B (1T tokens) fine-tuned on 10B tokens (7B model: 3B tokens) at 8k context. Memory layers are {6,12,18}. The task is the passkey task from Mohtashami and Jaggi 2023.
  - quote: "achieving 94.5% accuracy at a context length of 100k and 73% at 256k tokens, while the baseline is unable to handle context longer than its training length (2k)."
  - where: Fig. 1 caption, p.2; §4.2.

- Claim: More few-shot demonstrations in a longer context improve TREC accuracy a lot and WebQS a little.
  - number: LongLLaMA 3B TREC 67.0 (2K) → 73.3 (8K). 7B TREC 63.2 → 75.9. WebQS 3B 21.2 → 22.4. WebQS 7B 25.5 → 27.7.
  - setup: demonstrations fill the context up to the given length, 20 sampling trials averaged. TREC has 50 classes and only about 100 examples fit in 2K, so a class may be missing entirely.
  - quote: "2K 67.0 63.2 21.2 25.5 … 8K 73.3 75.9 22.4 27.7"
  - where: Table 1, p.7.

- Claim: At the same 4K fine-tuning budget FoT beats standard long-context fine-tuning, and it can still use context beyond its training length. The baseline is capped at 4K.
  - number: TREC at 4K, 60.9 (FoT) vs 57.2 (baseline). FoT reaches 62.5 at 8K. WebQS at 4K, 21.0 vs 18.7. At 2K, WebQS is 20.8 (FoT) vs 20.7 (baseline).
  - setup: 3B models, 1B fine-tuning tokens, 4K context.
  - quote: "2K 52.8 55.6 20.7 20.8 / 4K 57.2 60.9 18.7 21.0 / 6K – 61.7 – 21.2 / 8K – 62.5 – 20.7"
  - where: Table 2, p.7.

- Claim: Long-context fine-tuning with FoT does not degrade short-context performance.
  - number: LM Evaluation Harness average score 0.53 vs 0.53 (3B) and 0.55 vs 0.55 (7B).
  - setup: LongLLaMA evaluated without context extension, against OpenLLaMA.
  - quote: "Average score 0.53 0.53 0.55 0.55"
  - where: Table 5, App. A.4, p.17.

- Claim: On Qasper, LongLLaMA 3B improves as context grows, and is roughly on par with LongChat 7B.
  - number: LongLLaMA 3B 18.7 (2K), 20.7 (4K), 23.2 (6K), 26.6 (8K). LongChat 7B 19.4, 21.2, 25.0, 28.8.
  - setup: zero-shot, Qasper validation set (SCROLLS), Harness implementation.
  - quote: "Context length OpenLLaMA 3B LONGLLAMA 3B LLaMA 7B LongChat 7B / 2K 18.7 18.7 18.7 19.4 … 8K - 26.6 - 28.8"
  - where: Table 6, p.18.

- Claim: A small model fine-tuned with FoT on 2K total context keeps gaining perplexity up to 64K tokens. It matches Transformer-XL at 2K and beats the Memorizing Transformer (MT) at every length.
  - number: FoT 2K → 64K: GitHub 6.72 → 5.32, Isabelle 5.63 → 4.44, arXiv 8.17 → 6.81, PG-19 23.74 → 22.65. MT at 64K: 7.26, 6.64, 8.60, 23.24. Transformer-XL at 2K: 6.85, 5.76, 8.21, 23.57.
  - setup: 184M model pre-trained 100k steps at 1K context on C4, then 10k fine-tuning steps with d=128, local context 1K. Zero-shot evaluation. MT and Transformer-XL fine-tuned from the same checkpoint (MT with 1K local context and 16K memory).
  - quote: "FOT enjoys steady perplexity gains up to 64K tokens, although it was fine-tuned only with the 2K total differentiable context length."
  - where: §5.2 and Table 3, pp.8–9.

- Claim: A 37M model trained on 512-token documents retrieves from a 16M-token memory on a synthetic dictionary-lookup task.
  - number: accuracy above 92% at 16M tokens. The baseline Transformer fails by 16K tokens.
  - setup: after 5k steps. Local context 256, k=32 retrieved keys, d raised from 1 to 128 once the model reaches 98% training accuracy. Error bars are min/max over 10 seeds.
  - quote: "FOT, after 5k steps of training, can effectively utilize memory consisting of 16M tokens achieving accuracy above 92%."
  - where: §5.2 p.9; Fig. 10 and App. F.

- Claim: In the multi-document setting, a larger d gives better perplexity. Perplexity grows only gracefully with memory size.
  - number: +0.18 perplexity when memory scales to more than 500k tokens (standard FoT variant).
  - setup: PG-19, memory of multiple books, 184M model. Single-doc MT serves as a soft lower bound (Fig. 8).
  - quote: "In the standard variant of FOT (bold line), the perplexity increases only by 0.18 when scaling to > 500k tokens."
  - where: §5.3, p.9.

- Claim: Negatives and differentiable keys and values both matter.
  - number: no negatives (d=1) degrades perplexity as context grows (Fig. 6, no number in the text). Single-doc PG-19, FoT d=1 vs MT: 14.18 vs 14.68 (512), 14.17 vs 14.46 (1024), 14.11 vs 14.43 (2048).
  - setup: PG-19 ablations.
  - quote: "the lack of negatives in training (d = 1) results in a significant deterioration in model perplexity when the context length grows."
  - where: App. C.1, C.2 and Table 8, p.22.

- Claim: Dense attention over the whole memory gave only marginal differences from kNN retrieval. The authors replaced the MT gating with a simpler mechanism and found no performance difference.
  - number: none.
  - setup: used in LongLLaMA. Exact kNN via FAISS in the other experiments.
  - quote: "we use dense attention instead of the kNN retrieval, as we found only marginal performance differences, and it is simpler to implement."
  - where: §4.1, p.6; App. C.3.

LIMITS
- The authors list scaling context as the most important open problem. Storing more than 16M (key, value) pairs needs a distributed multi-node system. Exact kNN does not scale, and approximate kNN would need engineering and a check of its effect on quality (§6, p.10).
- d was capped at 64 or 128 by single TPUv3/v2 memory. Crossbatch raises training cost, but only in a subset of layers.
- Hard-negative mining and other contrastive methods are left as future work. Combining FoT with other long-context methods is also left open.
- Passkey retrieval is a synthetic task, and so are dictionary lookup and the perplexity analyses. The only real downstream tasks are TREC, WebQS and Qasper. These were measured only on 3B and 7B OpenLLaMA models.
- The Qasper table shows LongLLaMA 3B below LongChat 7B at 4K–8K. I read this as a model-size difference but the paper does not say so.
- Dated: the base models are OpenLLaMA 3B/7B with 2K native context, from 2023. The comparison methods are Position Interpolation, Landmark attention and MT, so the results predate native long-context models.
- Attention is applied only in a handful of memory layers. LongLLaMA uses dense attention, not kNN, so the 256k result does not test kNN at that scale.
- The distraction-issue evidence is measured on a small 184M model.

BUILDS ON: Memorizing Transformer (Wu et al., 2022) for the kNN memory layer. Contrastive learning, via CLIP (Radford et al., 2021), SimCLR (Chen et al., 2020), batch-size scaling (Gao et al., 2021b) and TRIME (Zhong et al., 2022). Transformer-XL (Dai et al., 2019). Passkey retrieval (Mohtashami and Jaggi, 2023). Few-shot setup (Hao et al., 2022). NoPE (Haviv et al., 2022). OpenLLaMA (Geng and Liu, 2023). RedPajama. Also compared against RETRO (Borgeaud et al., 2022) and Position Interpolation (Chen et al., 2023).

CODE: Listing 1 (p.10) is a JAX crossbatch sketch. Key lines:
- `pkey_fst = pos_encode_as_first(xk = key)` encodes keys from other contexts as if at position 0.
- `cross_batch_keys = pkey_fst[cross_batch_selector[:, 1:]]` picks keys from other documents.
- `attention_keys = jnp.concatenate([pkey[:, None], cross_batch_keys], axis=1)`.

The extracted text is spaced oddly, so quote it from the PDF rather than the extraction. Full pseudocode is in Appendix L.

FIGURES
- Fig. 1 (p.2): passkey accuracy vs prompt length for LongLLaMA 3B and OpenLLaMA 3B. It shows the extrapolation cliff of the baseline at 2K in one picture.
- Fig. 2 (p.4): FoT overview with Cprev, Ccurr and the d−1 negative documents. It shows the crossbatch mechanism.
- Fig. 3 (p.5): positive attention mass vs number of documents, with a 1/d reference line. It shows the distraction issue directly.
- Fig. 10 (App. F): dictionary-lookup accuracy up to 16M tokens, FoT vs Transformer.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions in the PDF. Extraction was clean text but with some garbled spacing in the code listing and some inline math. All numbers I quote were checked against the extraction. I did not search the target note for FoT or Tworkowski citations. A grep for "focused|tworkowski|FoT" in `03-budgeting-the-window.md` returned no matches, so the paper is not yet cited there.
